ceiling_statement: The maximum feasible cross-legal-order generality is profile-parametricity: every trusted mechanism (admission, provenance, replay, certificates, structural validation, citation grammar, deontic classification) is a single function parameterized by a hash-committed legal-order PROFILE supplied as data (article ranges, gazette/publisher identity and key material, language/script normalization, calendar, citation grammar, deontic lexicon), with a noninterference guarantee that no trusted decision depends on any jurisdiction fact except through the profile parameter; any legal order lacking a committed well-formed profile yields typed UNKNOWN (H2), never a guess. No feasible system can exceed this: mechanism-level universality is attainable, semantic-level universality is not — there exists no jurisdiction-free formal semantics of law, so content decisions are necessarily relative to the profile's committed model.
derivation: Information-theoretic: a validator's output can carry no information about a jurisdiction's structure (how many constitution articles, what a gazette citation looks like, which calendar governs versioning) that was not supplied as input; if that information is not in the committed profile, a decision about it is fabrication — structurally forbidden by H2. Therefore full generality = moving ALL jurisdiction information out of code into committed data, and the ceiling on the code side is exactly parametricity/noninterference (two runs differing only in un-profiled jurisdiction facts must produce identical outputs or both UNKNOWN). Model-dependence is irreducible: deontic and structural semantics differ across legal orders (civil-law codified hierarchies vs common-law precedent, differing amendment/consolidation rules), so 'correct for legal order J' is only definable relative to a formal model of J — the profile schema IS that model, and a legal order inexpressible in the schema is honestly out of scope (UNKNOWN), which is the H2-optimal outcome, not a defect. Verification: the profile must be hash-committed into the release chain, else a producer could swap jurisdiction rules undetected, violating H8.
relativity_note: Relative to the committed legal-order profile SCHEMA — i.e., a chosen formal structural model of a legal order (FRBR/ELI work-expression-manifestation identity + gazette-anchored publication events + per-profile citation and deontic grammars, the model B0 already instantiates for Greece). Generality claims hold for exactly the class of legal orders expressible in this schema; anything outside it is typed UNKNOWN by construction.
attainment_mechanism: Buildable now, because B0's lower layers are already content-neutral (map row AX-22): the certificate schema authority-v2/schema/transition-certificate.cddl, the crypto/identity layers (Ed25519 chain in source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp, TUF roles authority-v2/roles/ROLES-MODEL.sexp), the Merkle/census/replay spine, and the ELI URI constructors carry no Greek constants. Attainment: (1) define a profile .sexp schema and extract every jurisdiction constant into a Greece profile — the constants are already localized and enumerable: greek-law-types.lisp registry (systems/orchestrator-omega-modules/greek-law-types.lisp), *constitution-articles*=120 in structure.lisp, FEK issue tables, /exp/ell URI segment, el/en language assertion, the revision calendar in historical.lisp, the #§ 1-9999 range in systems/orchestrator-engine-sbcl/adapters/raw-text-adapter.lisp; (2) hash the profile into artifact-census.lisp's chained census and make it an admission input under authority-v2/kernel/admission-model.sexp, so profile swap = new accountable transition (H6); (3) enforce parametricity structurally with a build gate in the proven pattern of tests/architecture-multiplicity-test.lisp / architecture-gate.lisp: a jurisdiction literal (article count, gazette code, language tag, calendar date rule) appearing in any trusted seat outside the single profile-loader seat fails the gate — one seat per concept (H4) applied to jurisdiction knowledge itself; (4) unknown jurisdiction => the profile loader returns typed UNKNOWN and every downstream gate fail-closed blocks (H2/H3). All in SBCL + SHA-256; no redesign of the neutral layers.
b0_gap: Map row AX-22 + §3: B0 is PARTIAL — the neutral layers exist, but domain validation is Greece-coupled in code: hardcoded 120 constitution articles (structure.lisp), FEK issue identifiers, /exp/ell path segment, el/en language assert, the revision calendar in historical.lisp, and the #§ 1-9999 adapter range; greek-law-types.lisp is a registry+config in the right direction but still a Greek-only seat compiled into the trusted path. The cross-order design exists only as deployment/LAWMAX-UNIVERSAL-SOURCE-CONTRACT.md — per the map an UNAPPROVED, FROZEN proposal with no executable enforcement (and per creator law it cannot self-activate; it awaits explicit approval). No profile schema, no profile-commitment into the release chain, and no parametricity gate exist today.
lean_obligation: Model trusted decision procedures as D : Profile -> Input -> Outcome with Outcome ::= PASS | FAIL | UNKNOWN, a well-formedness predicate WF : Profile -> Prop, and jurisdiction facts J partitioned into profiled(p) and unprofiled parts. Prove: theorem profile_noninterference : forall p x1 x2, WF p -> agree_on_profiled p x1 x2 -> D p x1 = D p x2 (no trusted decision reads un-profiled jurisdiction information), and theorem honest_unknown : forall p x, ¬ WF p -> D p x = UNKNOWN, and theorem profile_bound : Admit release -> committed_hash release.profile ∈ release.census_chain (the profile in force is offline-recomputable from the release chain, zero producer trust).
